claimed.text: At the press conference Greer claimed some 400 witnesses with first-hand experience who were willing to testify before Congress, and the Project called for hearings with subpoena power and amnesty for witnesses.

The Briefing Document's editorial header for Stone says he saw living and dead extraterrestrials on an Army team that retrieved crashed craft; in his own printed words he trained at an NBC school and served as an NBC non-commissioned officer in the 96th Civil Affairs Company. Fox News showed him at the May press conference saying he had been involved in recoveries of crashed saucers.

Daniel Sheehan served as the Project's counsel, to defend any witnesses who might be charged with breaking their security oaths, and told the press conference he had been shown UFO photographs bearing alien writing symbols in the National Archives during the Carter administration, which he traced onto a legal pad; no document was produced.
Callahan described the JAL incident at the conference, one of only five people an opened source places at that podium; the others are Stone, George Filer, Sheehan and Alfred Webre.

Other cohort testimonies: Karl Wolfe says that at an NSA facility on Langley AFB he was shown Lunar Orbiter photographs of the moon; Donna Hare, who says she worked in NASA's Building 8 for the contractor Philco Ford in 1970 and 1971, says a technician told her such things were always airbrushed out before images were released to the public; Don Phillips describes a 1966 or 1967 sighting at a classified radar site; and John Weygandt's testimony gives his Marine Corps service in detail. Hare's further accounts are relayed at second and third hand.
McCandlish, who describes himself as a conceptual artist for defence contractors, is the source in print of the names Alien Reproduction Vehicle and Flux Liner.

Warren's printed testimony places him with the 81st Tactical Fighter Wing at Bentwaters in December 1980, with his PRP clearance approved on 11 December. Stone told the Project that an Army team took him to Bentwaters in late December 1980.
How the claims reached us: for Jacobs the Briefing Document is the last and weakest anchor, because he had published under his own name in 1982 and 1989 before any interviewer sought him out.
Greer says he briefed the sitting CIA Director, R. James Woolsey, on UFOs at a dinner in December 1993.

John Podesta called publicly for declassification of UFO records at a National Press Club event organised by the Coalition for Freedom of Information in October 2002, seventeen months after Greer's event, and said on leaving the White House in 2015 that his biggest failure of the year was once again not securing the disclosure of the UFO files.

Herrera's own account is on a dated recording, a podcast episode of July 2023. AARO's historical report summarises an anonymous former service member's claim of seeing Special Forces load containers onto a craft in 2009; the board infers, without any record making the link, that this is Herrera.

contested.text: Corroboration inside the document is the compiler's own: Greer's notes tie his witnesses to each other, and the header saying Warren is corroborated by Nick Pope, Lord Hill-Norton and Clifford Stone cites two witnesses from the same document, one of them Stone.
A printed testimony is not a podium appearance. No opened source lists the twenty speakers, and nothing places Wolfe, Hare, Jacobs, Warren, Weygandt, Phillips or McCandlish at the 9 May 2001 podium.

Stone's service record, as Klass prints it from the National Personnel Records Center, runs clerk/typist, administration specialist, detachment sergeant and chief administrative clerk, with nothing supporting a recovery team; Stone himself filed a FOIA request about Bentwaters in December 1983 from his home address, without identifying himself as a serving sergeant. Kevin Randle, a thirty-year acquaintance working by a different method, records the same kind of discrepancies.

Wolfe's account places the imagery at Langley AFB, while NASA's catalogue says the programme was run from NASA Langley Research Center, a separate civil installation; his obituary mentions no Air Force service. The board declines the usual chronology objection, since the Briefing Document gives no year for his episode.
For Phillips nothing independent was found at all, and for Hare the employer is documented but her employment is not.

Warren's co-author repudiated their book in June 2017, alleging fabricated and altered documents, and the publisher suspended distribution in October 2017; the co-author still accepts as authentic Warren's January 1981 letter to his mother.
Woolsey and the other attendees disputed Greer's account of the 1993 dinner in a signed letter of September 1999, calling it a dinner party and his published account distorted.
Klass published a dated critique of the Project by name in Summer 2001 and recorded that Greer controlled admission to his events.
The promotional claim that Herrera is testifying to Congress is not supported by any opened record; he has never been a hearing witness.

record.text: The Briefing Document's title page names it as prepared for the press, the US government and the scientific community, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., Director, and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D., and dated April 2001.

Its section 3.8 prints sixty-eight dated testimony headings in five subsections, from radar and pilot cases to government insiders and technology. Sixty-five are dated between July 2000 and March 2001; Edgar Mitchell's is dated May 1998 and Vasily Alexeyev's March 1997; Gordon Cooper's, Denise McKenzie's and Phillip J. Corso's carry no date.

Every testimony carries an initials key naming Greer as interviewer, and his editorial comments are printed inside the witness text. In one bracketed note he writes that Mark McCandlish's testimony establishes that a UFO was stored at Norton AFB, beside a separate testimony from Lt Col John Williams saying he was never allowed in that area of the base, while adding that he could confirm the facility existed because he was responsible for the base's facilities in 1981-82.

Among the dated headings: John Callahan, October 2000; Clifford Stone, September 2000; Larry Warren, September 2000; Robert Jacobs, November 2000; Mark McCandlish, December 2000. Each is a record that the testimony was given under that heading and date, and of nothing more.

ABC News reported on 9 May 2001 that Greer organised the event at the National Press Club at which about 20 former government workers came forward. Philip Klass wrote within weeks that its stated aim was to prompt a congressional hearing, and that Greer's book held transcripts of 69 witnesses, 20 of whom spoke briefly.

Klass did not attend: he says Greer had refused him admission to a similar event in 1997, so Klass's account of the conference rests largely on Greer's press releases and his 573-page book, though the records Klass obtained himself do not.

The Clinton Presidential Library's UFO FOIA collection 2006-0474-F consists mostly of documents sent to the White House by Greer as head of CSETI; the Clinton White House's UFO collections are external correspondence, not intelligence programme records.

The printed record of the House Oversight task force hearing of 9 September 2025 shows Rep. Eric Burlison entering testimonies he said Greer had given him, including Michael Herrera's. It is not a witness appearance: Herrera is on no committee witness list, and his name occurs once across the three hearing records, in that colloquy.

NASA's own catalogue states that the Lunar Orbiter programme was managed by NASA Langley Research Center, with Lunar Orbiter 1 photographing from 18 to 29 August 1966; and Ford's corporate history documents Philco-Ford as the contractor that bid for Mission Control at Houston in 1963.

summary.text: By published accounts Greer founded CSETI in 1990 and the Disclosure Project in 1993; the Project sought congressional hearings and amnesty for government witnesses willing to break their security oaths, and its two products in 2001 were the Briefing Document and the press conference a month later.

One interviewer collected the whole cohort: Greer conducted the interviews, printed his own comments inside the witness text, and cross-referenced his witnesses to each other in bracketed notes. On the board's rule the document therefore fixes who gave testimony and when, and is Tier 2 at best for what the testimony says.

The board has checked eight of the sixty-eight against independent records, with mixed results: Clifford Stone's service record, as Philip Klass printed it, contradicts his account, Robert Jacobs had published his own years earlier, and John Callahan's case has a federal file that owes nothing to the Project.

The Project's material travelled on: most of the Clinton White House UFO file consists of documents Greer sent it, and in 2025 a congressman entered into a hearing record testimonies he said Greer had given him.
